title: Meet the Homeless Coalition's CEO Alexandria Ayala - NewsBreak
text:
By Abigail Duffy ,
11 hours ago Alexandria Ayala, CEO of the Homeless Coalition of Palm Beach County. Photo by Capehart When Alexandria Ayala was elected to the Palm Beach County School Board in 2020 as its youngest member ever and first Hispanic woman, she was excited to give back to the community that had shaped her. Three years into the job, Ayala was shocked to learn that there were nearly 6,000 children in the district who were sleeping on couches, living in cars, or huddling under bridges at night.
“I felt almost ignorant,” Ayala recalls of that moment in 2023. “The face of homelessness had changed. And I just couldn’t stand that it was the most vulnerable in our community.”
Disturbed by the data, Ayala volunteered on the board of the Homeless Coalition of Palm Beach County , a 40-year-old nonprofit that aims to prevent and end homelessness in the county. In February 2025, she became the Homeless Coalition’s chief executive officer, working in an interim capacity before officially taking on the role in October.
Given the Homeless Coalition’s relatively small size—it has a full-time staff of three—one of Ayala’s early objectives has been to focus the organization’s efforts toward supporting and convening with partners that can provide direct services to the area’s homeless population. “Collaboration is my favorite word,” she says. “We can empower our partners who have larger staffs and who oversee properties.”
With proceeds from its two signature fundraisers (the Senator Philip D. Lewis Bruncheon and The Mayor’s Ball, which is slated for August 29), the Homeless Coalition can disburse money quickly to fund organizational partners in the community that specialize in homelessness response as well as support shelters with resources such as new bike racks or supplies like Mylar blankets. It can also help people get on their feet by covering security deposits, move-in costs, and furniture for their new housing unit.
“I’ve assembled regular meetings with the leads of other organizations we work with so we can get the pulse of what’s working and what’s not so we can decide how to allocate money,” Ayala explains. “Instead of this being a confusing, case-by-case, client-by-client thing, we’re going to give you a bulk amount. You have one year to use it, and if the purpose changes, you let me know.”
By simplifying and staying focused, the team at the Homeless Coalition can keep tabs on any advocacy or legislation that impacts its work in the area. Marketing and raising awareness are part of that, Ayala says, adding that she wants locals to understand that the person who just helped them checkout at Publix might be unhoused.
“Everyone loves Palm Beach County,” she says. “We have the slogans, we have the attraction of wealth, we have all these exciting things happening. Everything that makes this county what it is relies on the people who sustain it for us, and that’s our workforce. They deserve a good life if they work for it.
The post Meet the Homeless Coalition’s CEO Alexandria Ayala appeared first on Palm Beach Illustrated .
